experiment_description: A liquid-crystal-integrated Mach-Zehnder interferometer (LC-MZI) was fabricated on a silicon-nitride-on-insulator photonic platform for classical optical characterization. The photonic layer was LPCVD SiN with 300 nm height, fully etched through 300 nm, patterned into 1 µm-wide waveguides and covered by a 2 µm PECVD SiO2 upper cladding. The LC interaction region consisted of a trench opened in the SiO2 cladding above the waveguide, with trench width 3 µm and modulator length L = 500 µm. The trench was filled with nematic liquid crystal E7 after assembly of SU-8 microfluidic walls and a rubbed-polyimide-coated quartz lid; Cr/Au electrodes supplied an AC square-wave voltage to reorient the LC molecules. Both balanced and unbalanced MZI layouts were made from two 2×2 multimode interferometers. Static spectra were measured by wavelength sweep: for the unbalanced MZI, output port S42 was monitored over 1500–1600 nm while the LC drive amplitude was varied from zero until a half-wave phase shift of the interference fringe was obtained; for the balanced MZI, output port S32 was monitored over 1540–1580 nm while the voltage was swept through the optical switching transition. The half-wave voltage Vπ was extracted from the voltage-induced fringe shift. The extinction ratio was extracted from the balanced-MZI maximum-to-minimum transmission contrast. Dynamic modulation was measured on the unbalanced MZI at fixed wavelength 1549.2 nm, corresponding to a constructive interference condition before voltage application, using a 1 kHz square-wave drive with amplitude equal to the extracted switching voltage; rise and fall times were read from the optical transient.

unbalanced_mzi_half_wave_voltage_v.description: Measured voltage required to induce a π phase shift in the 500 µm LC phase modulator of the unbalanced LC-MZI.

unbalanced_mzi_vpi_length_product_v_mm.description: Half-wave voltage-length product for the 500 µm unbalanced LC-MZI phase modulator, derived from the measured half-wave voltage and modulator length.

balanced_mzi_half_wave_voltage_v.description: Measured voltage required to switch the balanced LC-MZI by a π phase shift using the 500 µm LC phase modulator.

balanced_mzi_extinction_ratio_db.description: Measured maximum-to-minimum optical transmission contrast of the balanced LC-MZI during voltage-controlled phase tuning.

rise_time_ms.description: Measured optical rise time of the LC-MZI transmission transient under a 1 kHz square-wave drive at the switching-voltage amplitude.

fall_time_ms.description: Measured optical fall time of the LC-MZI transmission transient under a 1 kHz square-wave drive at the switching-voltage amplitude.

experiment_description: Two-photon quantum interference was measured using an electron-beam-defined LC-MZI chip with the same SiN/SiO2/E7 liquid-crystal phase-shifter platform: 300 nm-thick fully etched SiN waveguides of 1 µm width, a 3 µm-wide LC trench above the waveguide, a 500 µm LC modulation length, SU-8 LC cell walls, a rubbed-polyimide quartz lid, and AC voltage drive applied to Cr/Au electrodes. Photon pairs were generated by spontaneous parametric down-conversion in a 7 mm-long type-II periodically poled potassium titanyl phosphate crystal pumped by a 780 nm continuous-wave tunable diode laser. The orthogonally polarized photons were separated by a polarizing beam splitter; residual pump light was removed with long-pass filters; polarization in each arm was prepared with half-wave and quarter-wave plates. A translation stage in one arm controlled the relative photon delay. Photons were coupled into and out of the integrated LC-MZI using four lensed fibers, with polarization controllers used to optimize collection. Output photons were detected by superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors, and arrival times were recorded with a quTAG time-to-digital converter for time-correlated single-photon-counting coincidence analysis. First, photon-pair indistinguishability was checked using a fiber beam splitter by scanning the relative delay and computing Hong-Ou-Mandel visibility after accidental-coincidence correction. For the on-chip experiment, photon pairs were injected into both LC-MZI inputs; the voltage-dependent two-photon coincidence was measured at zero relative path delay τ = 0 while sweeping the LC voltage. Full delay-line sweeps were then performed with the LC drive held fixed at 1.06 V, 1.22 V, and 1.40 V to extract voltage-dependent two-photon interference visibility from the coincidence dip depth.

fiber_beam_splitter_hom_visibility_perce.description: Accidental-corrected Hong-Ou-Mandel visibility of the photon-pair source measured before injection into the integrated chip using a fiber beam splitter.

on_chip_two_photon_visibility_at_1p06_v_.description: Two-photon interference visibility measured on the LC-MZI from a full delay-line sweep with the LC phase-shifter voltage held at 1.06 V.

on_chip_two_photon_visibility_at_1p22_v_.description: Two-photon interference visibility measured on the LC-MZI from a full delay-line sweep with the LC phase-shifter voltage held at 1.22 V.

on_chip_two_photon_visibility_at_1p40_v_.description: Two-photon interference visibility measured on the LC-MZI from a full delay-line sweep with the LC phase-shifter voltage held at 1.40 V.

experiment_description: A wafer-scale version of the LC-integrated SiN photonic platform was fabricated on a 4-inch wafer using i-line stepper lithography rather than electron-beam lithography. SiN waveguides were formed by reactive-ion etching and covered with PECVD SiO2 cladding; an LC trench was opened above the waveguide, Cr/Au electrodes were defined, SU-8 walls formed the LC cell, and a rubbed-polyimide quartz lid was bonded before capillary injection of nematic E7 liquid crystal. In this scalable design, the electrode structures were physically isolated from the LC trench to reduce electrical shorts and material degradation. Electro-optic characterization was performed on an unbalanced MZI fabricated by this stepper process. The tested device had an LC modulator length of 2000 µm and an electrode gap of 5 µm. Transmission spectra were recorded by sweeping wavelength from 1500 to 1600 nm at zero applied voltage and under LC drive, and the switching behavior was also monitored as normalized transmitted power versus voltage at a fixed wavelength of 1557 nm while the voltage was swept over the switching range. The half-wave voltage was extracted from the voltage required to shift the MZI transmission by one π phase condition.

stepper_device_half_wave_voltage_v_2000u.description: Measured half-wave voltage for the stepper-lithography LC-MZI with 2000 µm LC modulation length and 5 µm electrode gap.

stepper_device_vpi_length_product_v_mm_2.description: Voltage-length product derived from the measured half-wave voltage of the stepper-lithography LC-MZI with 2000 µm modulation length and 5 µm electrode gap.
